Natural Language Processing: We present BERT, a bidirectional transformer encoder pre-trained on masked language modeling and next sentence prediction, which achieves state-of-the-art results on question answering, named entity recognition, and natural language inference benchmarks.

This paper introduces a neural machine translation system based on the transformer architecture with multi-head self-attention, achieving BLEU improvements over recurrent sequence-to-sequence models while training significantly faster.
We propose an extractive summarization framework that scores sentences using contextual word embeddings and a graph-based ranking algorithm, producing concise summaries of long documents.
We train large language models on trillions of tokens and study scaling laws relating model size, dataset size, and compute to downstream task performance including reasoning and code generation.
We introduce a tokenization-free approach to part-of-speech tagging and dependency parsing using character-level convolutional networks, reducing the need for language-specific preprocessing.

This work explores prompt-based few-shot learning, where a pretrained language model adapts to new tasks through natural language instructions and a small number of exemplars, without gradient updates.
We build a retrieval-augmented generation system that combines dense passage retrieval with a sequence-to-sequence model, allowing open-domain question answering to cite evidence passages.
We develop a multilingual embedding space aligned across 100 languages using aligned corpora, supporting zero-shot cross-lingual transfer for classification and retrieval tasks.
We evaluate sentiment analysis and aspect-based opinion mining using a hierarchical attention network over word and sentence encodings, improving accuracy on product review datasets.
We present a sequence labeling approach for named entity recognition combining bidirectional LSTM encoders with conditional random field decoders and subword embeddings.
Computer Vision: We propose a deep convolutional neural network architecture with residual connections that achieves top-1 accuracy on ImageNet classification while remaining efficient to train.
We introduce a two-stage object detector that proposes candidate regions with a region proposal network and classifies them with fully connected layers, achieving real-time performance.
We present a U-Net style encoder-decoder with skip connections for biomedical image segmentation, producing pixel-wise masks from limited training data.
We train a vision transformer that applies self-attention directly to image patches, matching convolutional baselines on image classification without inductive biases.
We develop a generative adversarial network that synthesizes high-resolution photorealistic images with progressively growing generator and discriminator architectures.
We address monocular depth estimation and semantic segmentation with a shared multi-task encoder, demonstrating improved generalization across driving datasets.
We propose a contrastive self-supervised learning framework that learns image representations by maximizing agreement between augmented views, matching supervised transfer performance.
We present a face detection and recognition pipeline combining multitask cascaded convolutional networks with facial landmark alignment for unconstrained images.
We introduce a diffusion model for image generation that iteratively denoises samples from a learned noise schedule, outperforming GANs in fidelity metrics like FID.
We design an instance segmentation method that extends object detection with a mask branch, segmenting every object instance in an image in a single forward pass.
Machine Learning Theory: We derive generalization bounds for neural networks via PAC-Bayesian analysis, relating sharpness of the loss landscape to expected risk on unseen data.
This paper proves convergence rates for stochastic gradient descent on smooth nonconvex objectives, establishing O(1/sqrt(T)) oracle complexity for finding stationary points.
We analyze the sample complexity of learning halfspaces under adversarial label noise, providing upper and lower bounds that match up to logarithmic factors.
We study the regularization effect of weight decay and dropout, showing equivalence between dropout and adaptive regularization in the variational Bayesian sense.
We establish uniform convergence bounds for kernel methods in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, linking the spectral decay of the kernel to statistical consistency.
We analyze implicit bias of gradient descent on overparameterized linear networks, showing convergence to minimum-norm solutions and margin maximization.
We prove that certain classes of neural networks with random features approximate kernels in the infinite-width limit, connecting deep learning to kernel theory.
We investigate the information-theoretic limits of active learning, deriving query complexity bounds for disagreement-based active learning strategies.
We provide a tight analysis of the regret of UCB-style bandit algorithms under sub-Gaussian reward distributions, matching the lower bound up to constants.
We develop a framework for differential privacy in empirical risk minimization, proving utility guarantees for objective perturbation and output perturbation mechanisms.
Reinforcement Learning: We introduce deep Q-learning with experience replay and target networks, enabling agents to play Atari games directly from pixel observations and a scalar reward.
We propose Proximal Policy Optimization, a policy gradient method that clips importance ratios to keep updates within a trust region, improving stability and sample efficiency.
We present an actor-critic algorithm that estimates advantage functions with generalized advantage estimation, achieving strong results on continuous control benchmarks like MuJoCo.
We model sequential decision making as a Markov decision process and study exploration strategies based on count-based intrinsic rewards and uncertainty estimation.
We train an agent for a two-player zero-sum game using self-play with value networks and policy improvement, mastering the game beyond human world champion level.
We develop a model-based reinforcement learning agent that learns a latent dynamics model and plans with imagination, outperforming model-free baselines on vision-based tasks.
We study off-policy evaluation in reinforcement learning, proposing importance sampling estimators with variance reduction for evaluating policies from logged data.
We introduce a reward shaping methodology that accelerates learning by providing dense potential-based shaping rewards without altering the optimal policy.
We propose hierarchical reinforcement learning with a manager and worker structure, where high-level policies set subgoals that low-level policies learn to achieve.
We address multi-agent reinforcement learning with centralized training and decentralized execution, enabling cooperative policies for tasks requiring coordination.
Systems and Networking: We present a distributed key-value store that achieves high availability with quorum-based replication, consistent hashing, and failure detection in a large cluster.
We design a scheduling system for data center workloads that combines bin packing with fairness, reducing completion times for latency-sensitive jobs.
We evaluate congestion control algorithms for high-bandwidth networks, comparing loss-based and delay-based approaches under dynamic link conditions.
We build a columnar storage engine with late materialization and compression, accelerating analytical queries on petabyte-scale datasets.
We propose a GPU-accelerated graph processing framework that partitions graphs to minimize communication overhead across cluster nodes.
We develop a just-in-time compiler for a dynamic language that specializes bytecode based on observed types, delivering near-native execution speeds.
We implement a reliable transport protocol with forward error correction and packet retransmission to improve throughput over lossy wireless links.
We introduce a container orchestration strategy that migrates stateful workloads across nodes with minimal downtime and consistent snapshots.
We design a caching layer for web workloads that uses machine-learned eviction policies, improving hit rates compared to LRU baselines.
We present a fault-tolerant consensus protocol with leader election and log replication, tolerating crash failures under the partial synchronous model.
Other: We present a usability study of voice assistants, analyzing how privacy concerns and feedback design affect user trust and adoption in smart home settings.
We propose a cryptographic protocol for secure multiparty computation that keeps inputs private while enabling joint statistical analysis across organizations.
We develop a machine learning model for protein structure prediction that combines multiple sequence alignments with geometric attention over amino acid residues.
We analyze fairness in algorithmic decision making, proposing metrics to detect disparate impact in lending and hiring systems built on predictive models.
We design an intrusion detection system that monitors network flows with anomaly detection, reducing false positives via ensemble classifiers.
We apply deep learning to drug discovery, screening molecular libraries with graph neural networks that predict binding affinity of candidate compounds.
We evaluate a recommender system for online education, personalizing course sequences based on learner engagement and prior knowledge assessment.
We build a speech recognition front-end that separates overlapping speakers using neural beamforming, improving accuracy in noisy meeting rooms.
We propose a blockchain-based provenance system that records supply chain events with tamper-evident logs and selective disclosure of business data.
We study epidemiological models of disease spread that incorporate mobility data from cellular networks, improving forecasts of outbreak trajectories.
